summary: Per-backend functions that shape driver kwargs. adapters/registry.py holds _AUTH_ADAPTERS, a (provider_type, AuthProfile class) → function table, and auth_adapter(), which resolves the most specific registered auth class along the MRO and raises TypeError for an ambiguous multiple-inheritance match. Auth adapters cover Trino (password/JWT/Kerberos), Snowflake (password/token/OAuth2/certificate), BigQuery (service account), Databricks, MSSQL (password/Windows/Azure AD), Redshift (password/IAM), MotherDuck (token), and a shared user/password adapter for ten SQL backends. Config-shaping adapters (mssql.host_fold, mysql.ssl_compose, snowflake.session_params) are attached to profiles through __adapters__.
extension_points: Add an auth path by adding a (provider_type, AuthProfile class) entry to _AUTH_ADAPTERS.
Add config shaping by writing a (profile, base) → dict function and declaring it in a profile's __adapters__.
lifecycle_notes: Trino and BigQuery adapters import their driver packages lazily inside the function.
BigQuery service-account INFO parsing redacts the secret in error messages and suppresses exception chaining.
documentation_hooks: Auth matrix: which AuthProfile types map to which driver kwargs per backend
risks: snowflake.oauth2 sends only ACCESS_TOKEN and ignores CLIENT_ID/SECRET/SCOPE (comment marks it 'smell #1').
Adapter functions in mssql.py/snowflake.py lack type annotations, unlike the other adapter files.
supported_auth on each spec and the _AUTH_ADAPTERS table must agree; consistency is enforced only by test_supported_auth_consistency.py.
